Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The umpires and players again make their way out to the middle. Ben Stokes leads his troops out to the field. Now then, Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul walk to the crease to open for India. Chris Woakes is with the new ball, ready to go. Let's play...
.... THIRD INNINGS ...

For India, Akash Deep inflicted the early damage on Day 2 and it was he who struck with the second new ball to break the Brook-Smith stand, putting a spring in the team’s step. Deep and Mohammed Siraj combined well to clean up the lower order and the tail, with Siraj finishing with an impressive six-wicket haul. Looking ahead, we have just under an hour left in the day, and it will be interesting to see how India approach the remainder of the day and their second innings, especially with a healthy 180-run lead to play with. Back in a bit.

It was essentially Harry Brook and Jamie Smith versus India, with the rest of the England lineup offering little resistance. Remarkably, the scorecard features as many as six ducks. Brook and Smith launched a counterattack in the morning session to shift the momentum and then showed maturity in the afternoon by nudging the ball around and rotating the strike when India played with their ego by bowling a defensive line. After Brook fell, it was a procession but Smith remained unbeaten on 184, the highest score by an English wicketkeeper in Test cricket.

Well, the second new ball was always going to be India’s best chance to seize control, and they certainly made it count. From 387 for 5, the hosts collapsed, losing their last 5 wickets for just 20 runs as India wrapped things up quickly to secure a commanding 180-run lead. Looking at it from an English perspective, it could have been far worse. They were 84/5 earlier in the day and still 503 runs adrift but then came that marathon 303-run stand that flipped the momentum.

OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Mohammed Siraj wraps up the tail with a 6-for and does the job brilliantly for India! He bowls it on a fuller length, just outside off. It lands and just cuts back into the batter. Shoaib Bashir plants his front foot out but decides to leave it and hears the death rattle as the ball smashes into the off stump. Mohammed Siraj leaps in the air in jubilation as he registers his best bowling figures in England in Tests. Bashir is the sixth English batter to get out on a duck in this innings. Jamie Smith remains unbeaten. But England slip down badly from 387/5 to 407 all out.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of the day. The umpires and the players are back on the field. Centurions Harry Brook and Jamie Smith are all set to resume their batting after the break and the Indians spread out to the field. Washington Sundar has the ball and Brook to face. Here we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

The second new ball is 5 overs away, and this upcoming phase could prove pivotal. India will be eager to break this partnership and get into the lower order, but they know it will not be easy. Brydon Carse and Chris Woakes frustrated them in Leeds, and the visitors will be mindful of that. The new ball can be a double-edged sword, as it travels quicker across the outfield, and Brook and Smith can capitalise if the bowlers are not precise. The third and final session of the day will begin at 8.30 pm IST (3 pm GMT). See you then!

Despite India’s disciplined approach, both Brook and Smith were content to play the waiting game and refrained from offering any loose shots. With in-out fields in place, they milked the singles with ease and kept the scoreboard ticking. The only real chance India managed to create was a tough one when Pant couldn’t hold on to an edge from Smith on 121.

Having taken a lot of tap from Jamie Smith and Harry Brook before lunch, the break seemed to have allowed India to regroup. They managed to keep the two batters relatively quiet in the first hour, with Prasidh Krishna in particular making a conscious effort to keep the ball away from the batters. Around the hour mark, the ball was changed after it went out of shape, but that didn’t bring about a change in fortunes for the tourists.

SESSION SUMMARY - 106 runs in 28 overs. A sedate session in terms of run-scoring, but still a dominant one for England. India will take some encouragement from the fact that they managed to keep the scoring in check. While the first session saw a brisk scoring rate of 6.37, it dropped to 3.79 in the afternoon as the bowlers applied more control.

... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Well then, another session in this second Test has flown by. The surface remains reasonably flat with no such moon-craters to trouble batters, but India will be alert, one more wicket could expose England’s lower order from one end. With a hefty lead in hand, India won’t mind England’s aggressive approach, especially if they can squeeze in a quiet phase to build pressure. That said, England has flipped the momentum in their favor and are mindful of what happened in the first innings. After all, the visitors were 211 for 5 before launching a marathon stand. Patience and partnerships might still be their best route back for India. With England still trailing by 338 runs, a very interesting post-Lunch session is on the cards. It will start at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT). Stay tuned.

As the sun baked the surface and the ball softened, batting grew more comfortable. Brook and Smith capitalized, and kept the scoreboard moving. India’s field began to spread, slips disappeared, and Gill was suddenly chasing the game. The pressure shift also threw the spinners off rhythm. Jadeja, in particular, resorted to bowling on a length rather than full, unable to consistently draw the batters forward. Jamie Smith got off to his century and the duo saw through the morning session, stamping their authority.

But Harry Brook wasn’t going to retreat. He took the challenge head-on, counterattacking with flair and finding a willing partner in Jamie Smith. This duo of Yorkshire and Surrey quickly shifted the tone of the morning, putting the fall of two big wickets behind them. Smith made a statement by hammering 23 runs off a single Prasidh Krishna over just before drinks. In just the first 12 overs of the day, England had piled on 83 runs, with both batters racing to their fifties. India were forced to pull back, bringing on Jadeja and Sundar to slow things down, but Brook and Smith kept the tempo high.

It looked barren for the bowlers on the first two days, and while the pitch still offered plenty for batters, India’s attack came out on Day 3 with a spark lit by their late success on Day 2. That fiery burst in the final session had clearly stirred something, and the momentum carried over. Mohammed Siraj led the charge with a sensational early spell, removing Joe Root, strangling him down leg, and then sending Ben Stokes back the very next ball with a nasty lifter. England slipped further down to 84/5, searching for stability.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 Overs, 172 Runs, 2 Wickets. What a thoroughly entertaining morning session this was! As called by the cricket pundits, the 'Moving Day' has indeed progressed at the rate of knots. The Indians started cockahoop with the ball, but ended the session finding breakthroughs as England painted it all red, scoring at a rate of 6.37. A true display of the 'Bazball' approach.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is pitchside with Jonathan Trott, who starts by pointing out some footmarks that could offer decent assistance to India’s spinners. He adds that the cooler conditions today might make things a bit more comfortable for England in terms of the cracks not opening. Discussing the rough patches, Trott notes a few areas that bowlers like Jadeja and Sundar will definitely be eyeing. As Deep moves to the other end, he highlights some straight cracks on the surface, which Trott acknowledges. Deep adds that while the cracks are visible, they may not open up much, and overall, it still looks like a good pitch to bat on.

Much like Headingley, the Edgbaston surface has so far been the batter's friend, though it has been slower and offered less bounce. The ball is 20 overs old, but there may still be something in it for the bowlers during the first hour. Brook, having already danced down the track to Siraj for a couple of boundaries on Day 2, will look to take the game on, while Root is expected to play the steady hand in their bid to rebuild. Joe Root and Harry Brook then came together to halt the slide and ensured no further damage was done before the day drew to a close.

Gill picked up right where he left off, first extending the partnership with Ravindra Jadeja and then forging another valuable stand with Washington Sundar. Their partnerships helped India steer clear of the collapses that plagued them in Leeds. Shubman Gill, the star on Day 2 and India's captain, is down for a chat. He says that he is still on a high and he hadn't even practiced his slip fielding in the past two days and is happy that he took that catch. On his knock, he says that when he came into bat, he was watchful and was on 30-40 odd off 100 balls and then had a chat with one of the coaches as he was disappointed with too many shots going straight to the fielders and was told to just make sure that he bats long and avoid any sort of a collapse. Adds that he has worked on his technique, and earlier on, he was getting starts but lost his focus at the peak time and he went back to the basics before this tour and focused on just making runs, which was missing a bit. Gill also informs that he started practicing even when the IPL was going on as the two formats require different skills and he wanted to be properly ready for this series. Reckons that you can go back to T20 cricket after playing Tests but coming into a Test match after playing plenty of T20s is difficult. On the playing surface, Gill says that as the ball starts to get old, it will get easier to bat, so it is important to keep hitting their lines and lengths for a prolonged period and frustrate the batters.

England's top order, having spent over 150 overs in the field, looked visibly drained and ragged in their responses. Siraj backed up Akash Deep with a probing spell, and England soon slumped to 25 for 3. Harry Brook, too, had a jittery start and survived a close appeal while on 1, but with the calming presence of Joe Root at the other end, the two Yorkshire men prevented any further loss of a wicket with an unbeaten 52-run stand.

England’s bowlers showed great commitment, but they might reflect on a missed opportunity in their plan of attack. Persisting with the short-ball tactic for long spells on a slow surface meant the stumps weren't on target. In contrast, India’s bowlers came out with a spring in their step, full of energy and fire. They hit their lengths from the outset and applied pressure straight away. The biggest challenge for India with the ball was stepping up in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah. But Akash Deep embraced the responsibility with a spirited burst, removing both Duckett and Pope, centurions in the last Test, within successive deliveries, setting the tone early.

The final session capped off a commanding day for India, with Shubman Gill once again at the center of gravity. Carrying the weight of past collapses, he batted with the awareness of someone who knew what was at stake. Calm and composed, he kept the innings on track alongside Washington Sundar, as the pair stitched together a gritty 144-run stand. Sundar eventually departed, having played his part in stretching the score ahead. Shortly after, Gill’s marathon knock came to an end at 269, India added only a few more before the innings wrapped up, having made England work through 151 punishing overs in the heat. Bashir picked up three, while Tongue and Woakes shared four between them.

Post-lunch, Gill found an able ally in Washington Sundar, whose calm presence at number eight gave India the cushion to build deeper. England rotated bowlers, brought in spin, and even took a punt with Brook, but nothing stopped the Indian captain’s charge. Gill converted his double ton into a majestic 250, leading India into Tea with unwavering control and a tail still intact. Gill also became the sixth Indian skipper to get past the 200-run mark in an inning and also walked past several records, leapfrogging some of the greatest names ever to have graced the sport of cricket.

Starting the day with a ball that refused to talk and a surface that invited run-making, Gill and Jadeja built steadily. The partnership went past 200, Jadeja collected his 23rd Test fifty, and runs flowed without resistance. England tried everything, from a prolonged short-ball ploy to strategic spread fields, but struggled to make inroads. Josh Tongue eventually broke through with a sharp lifter to remove Jadeja on 89, late in the morning, and minimal hints of turn and uneven bounce began to surface.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Wow, what a delivery from Akash Deep and Ollie Pope departs on the very first ball. Akash comes back to over the wicket for the right-hander and serves the ball right up on the off stump, forcing the batter to play at it. Pope makes the mistake of playing across the line and the ball just nips away off the deck and squares him up. The outside edge is found yet again and the ball goes quickly towards second slip. KL Rahul reacts well to his right but fails to pouch it on the first attempt. KL manages to keep his composure and snaffles it on the second attempt. England have been rocked early, 13 for 2 now as the other centurion from the previous match, Ollie Pope, departs for a golden duck.
